```{julia}
using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end
```

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

"""
    ttest_by(df, yvar, byvar; level=0.95, unequal=false)

Stata-style `ttest <yvar>, by(<byvar>)`. Defaults to equal-variance (pooled),
like Stata; pass `unequal=true` for Welch. Prints the two-group summary table,
the difference with its CI, and one- / two-sided p-values, then returns the
underlying HypothesisTests object.
"""
function ttest_by(df, yvar::Symbol, byvar::Symbol; level::Float64=0.95, unequal::Bool=false)
    mask = .!ismissing.(df[!, yvar]) .& .!ismissing.(df[!, byvar])
    y   = df[mask, yvar]
    bv  = [_rawval(v) for v in df[mask, byvar]]
    levs = sort(unique(bv))
    length(levs) == 2 || error("by() must have exactly 2 non-missing levels, got $(length(levs))")
    g0 = Float64.(y[bv .== levs[1]])
    g1 = Float64.(y[bv .== levs[2]])

    tt = unequal ? HypothesisTests.UnequalVarianceTTest(g0, g1) :
                   HypothesisTests.EqualVarianceTTest(g0, g1)

    function grow(x, lbl)
        n  = length(x); μ = Statistics.mean(x); σ = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : NaN
        se = σ / sqrt(n)
        tc = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(max(n-1, 1)), 1 - (1-level)/2)
        (; Group=string(lbl), Obs=n, Mean=μ, StdErr=se, StdDev=σ,
           CI_lo=μ - tc*se, CI_hi=μ + tc*se)
    end

    ci = HypothesisTests.confint(tt; level=level)
    rows = [grow(g0, levs[1]),
            grow(g1, levs[2]),
            grow(vcat(g0, g1), "combined"),
            (; Group="diff", Obs=length(g0)+length(g1),
                Mean=tt.xbar, StdErr=tt.stderr, StdDev=NaN,
                CI_lo=ci[1], CI_hi=ci[2])]

    println(unequal ? "Two-sample t test with unequal variances" :
                      "Two-sample t test with equal variances")
    _pt_compat(DataFrames.DataFrame(rows))

    Printf.@printf("\ndiff = mean(%s) - mean(%s)    t  = %.4f\n",
                   levs[1], levs[2], tt.t)
    Printf.@printf("Ho: diff = 0                   df = %g\n\n", tt.df)
    println("   Ha: diff < 0          Ha: diff != 0         Ha: diff > 0")
    Printf.@printf("Pr(T < t) = %.4f    Pr(|T| > |t|) = %.4f    Pr(T > t) = %.4f\n",
                   HypothesisTests.pvalue(tt; tail=:left),
                   HypothesisTests.pvalue(tt),
                   HypothesisTests.pvalue(tt; tail=:right))
    return tt
end

"""
    wald_test(model, vars; values=zeros(length(vars)))

Stata-style `test <varlist>` after a regression — joint Wald test of
H0: βⱼ = value[j] for each j in `vars`. Uses the model's vcov (so it
respects robust/cluster SE if fitted that way). Reports the F statistic
F(q, dof_resid) and p-value, like Stata's `test` after `regress`.
"""
function wald_test(model, vars::AbstractVector; values=zeros(length(vars)))
    β     = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V     = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    names = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    vs    = string.(vars)
    idx   = [findfirst(==(v), names) for v in vs]
    miss  = findall(x -> x === nothing, idx)
    isempty(miss) || error("variable(s) not found in model: $(vs[miss])")

    # Drop coefficients with non-finite β or vcov row (collinear / dropped),
    # mirroring Stata's `test`/`testparm` behaviour.
    vals = collect(values)
    bad  = findall(k -> !isfinite(β[idx[k]]) || any(!isfinite, V[idx[k], idx]),
                   eachindex(idx))
    if !isempty(bad)
        @warn "Dropping collinear / non-finite coefficient(s): $(vs[bad])"
        keep = setdiff(eachindex(idx), bad)
        vs, idx, vals = vs[keep], idx[keep], vals[keep]
    end
    isempty(vs) && error("No testable coefficients remain.")

    q     = length(vs)
    Rβ    = β[idx] .- vals
    W     = Rβ' * (V[idx, idx] \ Rβ)
    dfr   = StatsBase.dof_residual(model)
    Fstat = W / q
    p     = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(q, dfr), Fstat)

    println("Wald F test (respects model's vcov):")
    for (k, v) in enumerate(vs)
        Printf.@printf("  ( %d)  %s = %g\n", k, v, values[k])
    end
    Printf.@printf("\n       F( %d, %g) = %.4f\n", q, dfr, Fstat)
    Printf.@printf("            Prob > F = %.4f\n", p)
    return (; F=Fstat, df1=q, df2=dfr, p=p, chi2=W)
end

"""
    margins_dydx(model, df, varname; level=0.95)

Stata-style `margins, dydx(<varname>)` for a linear model fit on `df`.
Supports the common continuous×categorical form `varname + g + varname & g`:

    AME = β_varname + Σ_k (n_k / N) · β_{varname × g = k}

The delta-method SE uses the model's own vcov. If that vcov has non-finite
entries on the rows the AME depends on (common with degenerate `Vcov.robust()`
on sparse categoricals), the function transparently refits the same formula
with **classical OLS vcov** and uses that for the SE only — so the result
never returns NaN when the AME itself is defined. A flag in the output
indicates which vcov was used.
"""
function margins_dydx(model, df, varname::Symbol; level::Float64=0.95)
    β   = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V   = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    nm  = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    N   = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))
    vstr = string(varname)

    idx_main = findfirst(==(vstr), nm)
    idx_main === nothing && error("'$vstr' not found as a main effect in model")

    # Build weight vector so that AME = w'β
    # For a linear model with interactions: ∂E[y]/∂x = β_x + Σ_k β_{x×D_k} · P(D_k)
    # where P(D_k) = proportion of observations at level k.
    w = zeros(length(β))
    w[idx_main] = 1.0
    re_a = Regex("^\\Q$vstr\\E\\s*&\\s*(.+?):\\s*(.+)\$")
    re_b = Regex("^(.+?):\\s*(.+?)\\s*&\\s*\\Q$vstr\\E\$")
    for (i, n) in enumerate(nm)
        m = match(re_a, n); m === nothing && (m = match(re_b, n))
        m === nothing && continue
        factor_col = Symbol(String(m.captures[1]))
        level_str  = String(m.captures[2])
        hasproperty(df, factor_col) || continue
        col = df[!, factor_col]
        lev = tryparse(Float64, level_str)
        n_k = lev === nothing ?
              sum(!ismissing(v) && string(_rawval(v)) == level_str for v in col) :
              sum(!ismissing(v) && _rawval(v) == lev for v in col)
        w[i] = n_k / N
    end

    ame = LinearAlgebra.dot(w, β)

    # Delta-method SE: Var(w'β) = w' V w
    # If robust vcov has NaN, build X manually and compute HC1 sandwich.
    Vw = V * w
    vcov_label = "Robust"
    if !all(isfinite, Vw)
        # Manual X matrix construction (same approach as testparm).
        # Parse coefnames to identify: main effects, factor dummies, interactions.
        resp = Symbol(split(string(FixedEffectModels.formula(model).lhs), "(")[end] |>
                      s -> replace(s, ")" => ""))
        # Find all unique raw column names used
        all_cols = Symbol[]
        factor_cols = Symbol[]
        for n in nm
            n == "(Intercept)" && continue
            if occursin("&", n)
                # Interaction: "var1 & factor: level"
                parts = split(n, r"\s*&\s*")
                for p in parts
                    if occursin(":", p)
                        fc = Symbol(strip(split(p, ":")[1]))
                        fc in factor_cols || push!(factor_cols, fc)
                        fc in all_cols || push!(all_cols, fc)
                    else
                        s = Symbol(strip(p))
                        s in all_cols || push!(all_cols, s)
                    end
                end
            elseif occursin(":", n)
                fc = Symbol(strip(split(n, ":")[1]))
                fc in factor_cols || push!(factor_cols, fc)
                fc in all_cols || push!(all_cols, fc)
            else
                s = Symbol(strip(n))
                s in all_cols || push!(all_cols, s)
            end
        end
        push!(all_cols, resp)

        df_c = dropmissing(df, all_cols)
        nn = nrow(df_c)

        # Build X column by column, matching coefnames order
        X_cols = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
        cn_new = String[]
        for n in nm
            if n == "(Intercept)"
                push!(X_cols, ones(nn)); push!(cn_new, n)
            elseif occursin("&", n)
                # Interaction term
                parts = split(n, r"\s*&\s*")
                col_vec = ones(nn)
                for p in parts
                    p = strip(p)
                    if occursin(":", p)
                        fc, lv = strip.(split(p, ":"; limit=2))
                        vals = [_rawval(v) for v in df_c[!, Symbol(fc)]]
                        lev = tryparse(Float64, lv)
                        col_vec .*= lev === nothing ?
                            Float64.(string.(vals) .== lv) :
                            Float64.(vals .== lev)
                    else
                        col_vec .*= Float64.(df_c[!, Symbol(p)])
                    end
                end
                if sum(col_vec .!= 0) >= 2
                    push!(X_cols, col_vec); push!(cn_new, n)
                end
            elseif occursin(":", n)
                fc, lv = strip.(split(n, ":"; limit=2))
                vals = [_rawval(v) for v in df_c[!, Symbol(fc)]]
                lev = tryparse(Float64, lv)
                col_vec = lev === nothing ?
                    Float64.(string.(vals) .== lv) :
                    Float64.(vals .== lev)
                push!(X_cols, col_vec); push!(cn_new, n)
            else
                push!(X_cols, Float64.(df_c[!, Symbol(n)])); push!(cn_new, n)
            end
        end
        Xm = hcat(X_cols...)
        y_m = Float64.(df_c[!, resp])
        k_m = size(Xm, 2)

        # OLS + HC1
        β_m = Xm \ y_m
        û = y_m - Xm * β_m
        XtXi = LinearAlgebra.inv(Xm' * Xm)
        meat = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(û.^2) * Xm
        V = XtXi * meat * XtXi * (nn / (nn - k_m))

        # Rebuild w aligned to cn_new
        w = zeros(k_m)
        idx_m = findfirst(==(vstr), cn_new)
        idx_m !== nothing && (w[idx_m] = 1.0)
        for (i, n) in enumerate(cn_new)
            m2 = match(re_a, n); m2 === nothing && (m2 = match(re_b, n))
            m2 === nothing && continue
            factor_col = Symbol(String(m2.captures[1]))
            level_str  = String(m2.captures[2])
            hasproperty(df_c, factor_col) || continue
            col = df_c[!, factor_col]
            lev = tryparse(Float64, level_str)
            n_k = lev === nothing ?
                  sum(!ismissing(v) && string(_rawval(v)) == level_str for v in col) :
                  sum(!ismissing(v) && _rawval(v) == lev for v in col)
            w[i] = n_k / nn
        end
        ame = LinearAlgebra.dot(w, β_m)
        Vw = V * w
        vcov_label = "Robust"
    end
    se   = sqrt(max(LinearAlgebra.dot(w, Vw), 0.0))
    z    = se > 0 ? ame / se : NaN
    pval = se > 0 ? 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z))) : NaN
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    lo, hi = ame - crit*se, ame + crit*se

    # Stata-style output
    nobs_str = replace(string(N), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
    Printf.@printf("\nAverage marginal effects%40sNumber of obs = %s\n", "", nobs_str)
    Printf.@printf("Model VCE: %s\n", vcov_label)
    Printf.@printf("\nExpression: Linear prediction, predict()\n")
    Printf.@printf("dy/dx wrt:  %s\n", vstr)
    println("\n", "-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("             |            Delta-method\n")
    Printf.@printf("             |      dy/dx   std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   round(Int, 100*level))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10.6f  %10.6f   %5.2f   %5.3f    %10.5f  %10.5f\n",
                   vstr, ame, se, z, pval, lo, hi)
    println("-"^78)

    return (; ame, se, z, p=pval, ci=(lo, hi), w)
end

"""
    margins_eyex(model, df, varname; level=0.95)

Stata-style `margins, eyex(<varname>) atmean` for a linear model with no
interactions involving `varname`. Elasticity evaluated at the sample means:

    ey/ex = β_varname · (x̄ / ŷ(x̄))    where   ŷ(x̄) = x̄' β

The delta-method SE uses the model's own vcov. If that vcov has non-finite
entries on the rows the elasticity depends on, the function transparently
refits the same formula with **classical OLS vcov** and uses that for the
SE only — so it never returns NaN when the elasticity itself is defined.

Supported coefficient layouts: intercept, continuous main effects, and
categorical dummies of the form "colname: level". Complex interactions
with `varname` are ignored (with a warning).
"""
function _xbar_from_coefnames(nm, df)
    xbar = zeros(length(nm))
    N = DataFrames.nrow(df)
    for (i, n) in enumerate(nm)
        if n == "(Intercept)"
            xbar[i] = 1.0
            continue
        end
        sym = Symbol(n)
        if hasproperty(df, sym)
            col = df[!, sym]
            xbar[i] = Statistics.mean(Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in skipmissing(col))
            continue
        end
        m = match(r"^(.+?):\s*(.+)$", n)
        if m !== nothing
            col_sym = Symbol(String(m.captures[1]))
            lev_str = String(m.captures[2])
            if hasproperty(df, col_sym)
                col = df[!, col_sym]
                lev = tryparse(Float64, lev_str)
                xbar[i] = lev === nothing ?
                    count(!ismissing(v) && string(_rawval(v)) == lev_str for v in col) / N :
                    count(!ismissing(v) && _rawval(v) == lev for v in col) / N
                continue
            end
        end
        @warn "margins: could not resolve mean for coefficient '$n'; using 0."
    end
    return xbar
end

function margins_eyex(model, df, varname::Symbol; level::Float64=0.95)
    β   = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V   = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    nm  = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    vstr = string(varname)

    idx = findfirst(==(vstr), nm)
    idx === nothing && error("'$vstr' not found as a main effect in model")

    if any(occursin("$vstr &", n) || occursin("& $vstr", n) for n in nm)
        @warn "Interactions involving '$vstr' detected — margins_eyex ignores them; elasticity is based on β_$vstr only."
    end

    xbar = _xbar_from_coefnames(nm, df)

    yhat = LinearAlgebra.dot(xbar, β)
    x̄    = Statistics.mean(skipmissing(df[!, varname]))
    dydx = β[idx]
    ela  = dydx * x̄ / yhat

    # Delta-method gradient of ela = β[idx] · x̄ / (xbar'β):
    #   ∂ela/∂β = (x̄ / ŷ) · [e_idx - (β[idx]/ŷ) · xbar]
    w = zeros(length(β)); w[idx] = 1.0
    g = (x̄ / yhat) .* (w .- (dydx / yhat) .* xbar)

    used_classical = false
    Vg = V * g
    if !all(isfinite, Vg)
        @warn "vcov has non-finite entries on relevant rows; refitting with classical OLS vcov for SE."
        try
            m2 = FixedEffectModels.reg(df, StatsBase.formula(model))
            V  = StatsBase.vcov(m2)
            Vg = V * g
            used_classical = true
        catch e
            @warn "Classical refit failed: $e"
        end
    end
    se   = sqrt(max(LinearAlgebra.dot(g, Vg), 0.0))
    z    = ela / se
    pval = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    lo, hi = ela - crit*se, ela + crit*se

    Printf.@printf("margins, eyex(%s) atmean%s\n", vstr,
                   used_classical ? "  [SE from classical OLS fallback]" : "")
    header = ["ey/ex", "Std. err.", "z", "P>|z|",
              "$(round(Int, 100*level))% CI low", "$(round(Int, 100*level))% CI high"]
    row = permutedims([ela, se, z, pval, lo, hi])
    _pt_compat(row; header=header)
    return (; elasticity=ela, se, z, p=pval, ci=(lo, hi), used_classical_vcov=used_classical)
end

"""
    _design_matrix_from_df(nm, df)

Reconstruct an `n × length(nm)` design matrix by interpreting each coefficient
name. Handles `(Intercept)`, continuous main effects, and categorical dummies
of the form `"col: level"`. Unknown terms contribute a zero column (with a
warning).
"""
function _design_matrix_from_df(nm::Vector{String}, df)
    n = DataFrames.nrow(df)
    X = zeros(n, length(nm))
    for (i, name) in enumerate(nm)
        if name == "(Intercept)"
            X[:, i] .= 1.0
            continue
        end
        sym = Symbol(name)
        if hasproperty(df, sym)
            col = df[!, sym]
            X[:, i] .= [ismissing(v) ? 0.0 : Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in col]
            continue
        end
        m = match(r"^(.+?):\s*(.+)$", name)
        if m !== nothing
            col_sym = Symbol(String(m.captures[1]))
            lev_str = String(m.captures[2])
            if hasproperty(df, col_sym)
                col = df[!, col_sym]
                lev = tryparse(Float64, lev_str)
                X[:, i] .= lev === nothing ?
                    [!ismissing(v) && string(_rawval(v)) == lev_str ? 1.0 : 0.0 for v in col] :
                    [!ismissing(v) && _rawval(v) == lev ? 1.0 : 0.0 for v in col]
                continue
            end
        end
        @warn "imtest: could not reconstruct design column for '$name'; using zeros."
    end
    return X
end

"""
    imtest(model, df)

Stata-style `estat imtest` — Cameron & Trivedi's decomposition of White's
information matrix test. Prints the four chi² components (Heteroskedasticity,
Skewness, Kurtosis, Total) and returns them as a NamedTuple.

Implementation follows Cameron & Trivedi (2005) *Microeconometrics* §8.6.
Small numerical differences from Stata's `estat imtest` are expected owing
to different rank-adjustment and redundancy-handling conventions.
"""
function imtest(model, df)
    nm = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    X  = _design_matrix_from_df(nm, df)
    beta = StatsBase.coef(model)

    yname = try
        Symbol(string(model.formula.lhs))
    catch
        try Symbol(model.yname) catch _e2; Symbol(StatsBase.responsename(model)) end
    end
    ycol = df[!, yname]

    keep = .!ismissing.(ycol) .& .!any(isnan, X; dims=2)[:]
    X    = X[keep, :]
    y    = Float64.(collect(skipmissing(ycol[keep])))
    e    = y .- X * beta               # raw OLS residuals
    n, k = size(X)
    s2   = sum(abs2, e) / n            # MLE variance (divide by n, not n-k)

    # Non-intercept columns
    idx_nz = [i for i in 1:k if nm[i] != "(Intercept)"]
    p = length(idx_nz)
    Xp = X[:, idx_nz]                 # n × p  (no intercept)

    # Helper: n*(1 - RSS/USS) = Stata's n*R²_uncentered
    function nR2_unc(dep, Z)
        b   = Z \ dep
        res = dep .- Z * b
        uss = sum(abs2, dep)
        rss = sum(abs2, res)
        return uss > 0 ? n * (1 - rss / uss) : 0.0
    end

    # ── Heteroskedasticity (delta_1) ──
    # dep = e² − σ̂². Regressors = [1, Xp, cross-products of mean-centered Xp].
    # Drop collinear binary squared terms.
    Xp_c = Xp .- mean(Xp, dims=1)     # mean-centered regressors
    het_cols = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    for a in 1:p, b in a:p
        col = Xp_c[:, a] .* Xp_c[:, b]
        # Drop if x²=x (binary): squared term collinear with original
        if a == b && abs(cor(col, Xp[:, a])) > 0.9999
            continue
        end
        push!(het_cols, col)
    end
    Z_het = isempty(het_cols) ? hcat(ones(n), Xp) :
            hcat(ones(n), Xp, reduce(hcat, het_cols))
    dep_h = e.^2 .- s2
    H     = nR2_unc(dep_h, Z_het)
    df_H  = size(Z_het, 2) - 1

    # ── Skewness (delta_2) ──
    # dep = e³ − 3σ̂²e. Regressors = [1, Xp].
    dep_s = e.^3 .- 3.0 .* s2 .* e
    Z_skew = hcat(ones(n), Xp)
    S     = nR2_unc(dep_s, Z_skew)
    df_S  = p

    # ── Kurtosis (delta_3) ──
    # dep = e⁴ − 6σ̂²e² + 3σ̂⁴. Regressors = [1] (intercept only).
    dep_k = e.^4 .- 6.0 .* s2 .* e.^2 .+ 3.0 .* s2^2
    Z_kurt = ones(n, 1)
    K     = nR2_unc(dep_k, Z_kurt)
    df_K  = 1

    # ── Total ──
    IM    = H + S + K
    df_IM = df_H + df_S + df_K

    p_H  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(max(df_H, 1)),  H)
    p_S  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(max(df_S, 1)),  S)
    p_K  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df_K),           K)
    p_IM = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(max(df_IM, 1)), IM)

    println("\nCameron & Trivedi's decomposition of IM-test\n")
    println("-"^50)
    @printf("%20s | %10s %5s %10s\n", "Source", "chi2", "df", "p")
    println("-"^21, "+", "-"^28)
    @printf("%20s | %10.2f %5d %10.4f\n", "Heteroskedasticity", H, df_H, p_H)
    @printf("%20s | %10.2f %5d %10.4f\n", "Skewness", S, df_S, p_S)
    @printf("%20s | %10.2f %5d %10.4f\n", "Kurtosis", K, df_K, p_K)
    println("-"^21, "+", "-"^28)
    @printf("%20s | %10.2f %5d %10.4f\n", "Total", IM, df_IM, p_IM)
    println("-"^50)

    return (; H   = (chi2=H,  df=df_H,  p=p_H),
              S   = (chi2=S,  df=df_S,  p=p_S),
              K   = (chi2=K,  df=df_K,  p=p_K),
              total = (chi2=IM, df=df_IM, p=p_IM))
end

function boxcox_mle(df::DataFrame, depvar::Symbol, xvars::Vector{Symbol};
                    condition = nothing)
    dfb = dropmissing(df[:, vcat([depvar], xvars)])
    if condition !== nothing
        dfb = filter(condition, dfb)
    end
    y  = Float64.(dfb[!, depvar])
    X  = hcat(ones(nrow(dfb)), [Float64.(dfb[!, v]) for v in xvars]...)
    cn = [string.(xvars); "_cons"]
    n, k = size(X)
    sumlogy = sum(log.(y))

    bc(y, θ) = abs(θ) < 1e-8 ? log.(y) : (y.^θ .- 1.0) ./ θ

    function loglik(θ)
        yt  = bc(y, θ)
        β   = X \ yt
        rss = sum((yt .- X * β).^2)
        sig2 = rss / n
        return -n/2 * log(2π * sig2) - n/2 + (θ - 1) * sumlogy
    end

    opt = _optimize_compat(θ -> -loglik(first(θ)), [0.1], Optim.BFGS())
    th  = Optim.minimizer(opt)[1]

    yt  = bc(y, th)
    bhat = X \ yt
    rss = sum((yt .- X * bhat).^2)
    sig = sqrt(rss / n)
    llhat = loglik(th)

    h   = 1e-5
    d2  = (-loglik(th + h) + 2 * loglik(th) - loglik(th - h)) / h^2
    se_th = sqrt(max(1.0 / d2, 0.0))
    z_th  = th / se_th
    p_th  = 2 * (1 - cdf(Normal(), abs(z_th)))
    ci_lo = th - 1.96 * se_th
    ci_hi = th + 1.96 * se_th

    ll_restricted = Dict{Float64, Float64}()
    for t0 in (-1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        ll_restricted[t0] = loglik(t0)
    end

    nobs_str = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
    println("\nFitting full model\n")
    @printf("%54sNumber of obs   = %10s\n", "", nobs_str)
    @printf("%54sLR chi2(%d)      = %10.2f\n", "", 1, -2*(loglik(0.0) - llhat))
    @printf("Log likelihood = %.3f%23sProb > chi2     = %10.3f\n",
            llhat, "", 1 - cdf(Chisq(1), -2*(loglik(0.0) - llhat)))
    println(" ")
    println("-"^78)
    @printf("%11s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
            string(depvar))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    @printf("      /theta | %10.7f  %10.7f  %6.2f   %5.3f    %10.7f  %10.7f\n",
            th, se_th, z_th, p_th, ci_lo, ci_hi)
    println("-"^78)
    println(" ")
    println("Estimates of scale-variant parameters")
    println("-"^28)
    @printf("             | Coefficient\n")
    println("-"^13, "+-", "-"^13)
    println("Notrans      |")
    for (j, v) in enumerate(xvars)
        @printf("%12s | %10.7f\n", v, bhat[j + 1])
    end
    @printf("%12s | %10.6f\n", "_cons", bhat[1])
    println("-"^13, "+-", "-"^13)
    @printf("      /sigma | %10.6f\n", sig)
    println("-"^28)
    println(" ")
    println("-"^57)
    @printf("   Test         Restricted     LR statistic\n")
    @printf("    H0:       log likelihood       chi2       Prob > chi2\n")
    println("-"^57)
    for t0 in (-1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        ll0 = ll_restricted[t0]
        lr  = 2 * (llhat - ll0)
        p   = 1 - cdf(Chisq(1), lr)
        @printf("theta = %2d   %14.3f   %10.2f         %7.3f\n",
                Int(t0), ll0, lr, p)
    end
    println("-"^57)

    return (; theta = th, se_th, beta = bhat, sigma = sig, loglik = llhat, nobs = n,
              xnames = cn, ll_restricted)
end

"""
    estat_hettest(model, df; vars=nothing, iid=false, mtest=false)

Breusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity.
Replicates Stata's `estat hettest [varlist] [, iid] [, mtest]`.

- No `vars`:  test against fitted values (1 df).
- With `vars`: test against the listed variables (joint + individual).
- `iid=true`:  uses the NR^2 form (regress u^2/s^2 on z; LM = n*R^2)
               matching Stata's `estat hettest, iid`.
- `iid=false` (default): uses the score form (Koenker, 1981) which is
               robust to non-normal errors — this is Stata's default.
- `mtest=true`: also reports Bonferroni and Sidak adjusted p-values
               for each variable individually.
"""
function estat_hettest(model, df;
                       vars::Union{Nothing, Vector{Symbol}} = nothing,
                       iid::Bool = false,
                       mtest::Bool = false)
    beta = StatsBase.coef(model)
    nm   = StatsBase.coefnames(model)
    n    = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))

    # Get fitted values and residuals
    # Build yhat from coefficients and data
    yhat = zeros(n)
    uhat = zeros(n)

    # Use dropmissing on needed columns
    needed = Symbol[]
    for name in nm
        name == "(Intercept)" && continue
        s = Symbol(strip(split(name, ":")[1]))
        hasproperty(df, s) && push!(needed, s)
    end
    resp = Symbol(split(string(FixedEffectModels.formula(model).lhs), "(")[end] |>
                  s -> replace(s, ")" => ""))
    push!(needed, resp)
    unique!(needed)
    dfc = dropmissing(df, needed)

    # Predict using FixedEffectModels
    yhat = FixedEffectModels.predict(model, dfc)
    uhat = Float64.(dfc[!, resp]) .- yhat

    sigma2 = sum(uhat.^2) / n     # MLE variance (divide by n)

    if vars === nothing
        z = hcat(ones(n), yhat)
        varnames = ["Fitted values"]
        q = 1
    else
        z = hcat(ones(n), [Float64.([_rawval(x) for x in dfc[!, v]]) for v in vars]...)
        varnames = string.(vars)
        q = length(vars)
    end

    # Helper: compute BP chi2 for given dep variable and regressors
    function _bp_chi2(dep, z, is_iid)
        b = z \ dep
        fitted = z * b
        if is_iid
            # Koenker (iid) form: n * R^2 of e^2 on z
            ss_tot = sum((dep .- mean(dep)).^2)
            ss_res = sum((dep .- fitted).^2)
            return ss_tot > 0 ? n * (1 - ss_res / ss_tot) : 0.0
        else
            # Normal (default) form: h = e^2/sigma^2, regress h on z, chi2 = ESS/2
            # Equivalently: ESS of e^2 on z, divided by 2*sigma^4
            ess = sum((fitted .- mean(dep)).^2)
            return ess / (2 * sigma2^2)
        end
    end

    chi2 = _bp_chi2(uhat.^2, z, iid)
    pval = 1 - cdf(Chisq(q), chi2)

    # Print Stata-style output
    form = iid ? "i.i.d." : "Normal"
    if mtest && vars !== nothing && length(vars) > 1
        # mtest format: individual + simultaneous table
        println("\nBreusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity")
        @printf("Assumption: %s error terms\n", form)
        println("H0: Constant variance\n")
        println("-"^38)
        @printf("    Variable |      chi2   df        p\n")
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^24)

        dep_sq = uhat.^2
        for v in vars
            zj = hcat(ones(n), Float64.([_rawval(x) for x in dfc[!, v]]))
            chi2_j = _bp_chi2(dep_sq, zj, iid)
            p_j = 1 - cdf(Chisq(1), chi2_j)
            @printf("%12s | %9.2f    1   %.4f*\n", v, chi2_j, p_j)
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^24)
        @printf("Simultaneous | %9.2f    %d   %.4f\n", chi2, q, pval)
        println("-"^38)
        println("* Unadjusted p-values")
    else
        # Standard format: single test
        var_label = vars === nothing ? "Fitted values of $(resp)" : join(varnames, ", ")
        println("\nBreusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity")
        @printf("Assumption: %s error terms\n", form)
        println("Variable: $(var_label)")
        println("\nH0: Constant variance\n")
        @printf("    chi2(%d) = %6.2f\n", q, chi2)
        @printf("Prob > chi2 = %.4f\n", pval)
    end

    return (; chi2, df = q, p = pval)
end
```

```{julia}
=#
# Two-way table with row/col percentages + chi-squared
ct = DataFrames.unstack(combine(groupby(df3, [:female, :suppins]), nrow => :freq),
             :female, :suppins, :freq)
println("Frequencies:")
println(ct)

# Chi-squared test of independence (manual — avoids Missing-typed matrix)
M_raw = Matrix(ct[:, Not(:female)])
M = Int.(coalesce.(M_raw, 0))           # drop Missing, cast to Int
n  = sum(M)
row_t = sum(M, dims = 2)
col_t = sum(M, dims = 1)
expected = (row_t * col_t) ./ n
χ² = sum((M .- expected).^2 ./ expected)
df_χ = (size(M, 1) - 1) * (size(M, 2) - 1)
@printf("Pearson chi-squared(%d) = %.4f, p = %.4f\n",
        df_χ, χ², 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df_χ), χ²))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Summary statistics obtained using command tabstat
tabstat totexp ltotexp, stat (count mean p50 sd skew kurt) col(stat)
=#
# Summary statistics: count, mean, p50, sd, skewness, kurtosis
function tabstat(x)
    xc = collect(skipmissing(x))
    return (count = length(xc),
            mean  = Statistics.mean(xc),
            p50   = Statistics.median(xc),
            sd    = Statistics.std(xc),
            skew  = StatsBase.skewness(xc),
            kurt  = StatsBase.kurtosis(xc) + 3)
end
let s1 = tabstat(df3.totexp), s2 = tabstat(df3.ltotexp)
    DataFrames.DataFrame(
        var   = ["totexp", "ltotexp"],
        count = [s1.count, s2.count],
        mean  = [s1.mean,  s2.mean],
        p50   = [s1.p50,   s2.p50],
        sd    = [s1.sd,    s2.sd],
        skew  = [s1.skew,  s2.skew],
        kurt  = [s1.kurt,  s2.kurt],
    )
end
```

### 3.4.3 Hypothesis tests

```{julia}
#=
* Wald test of equality of coefficients
quietly regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female ///
  income, vce(robust)
test phylim = actlim
=#
# Wald test of equality of coefficients: phylim = actlim
β  = StatsBase.coef(reg1); V = StatsBase.vcov(reg1); cnames = StatsBase.coefnames(reg1)
i_phylim = findfirst(==("phylim"), cnames)
i_actlim = findfirst(==("actlim"), cnames)
diff_est = β[i_phylim] - β[i_actlim]
se_diff  = sqrt(V[i_phylim, i_phylim] + V[i_actlim, i_actlim] -
                2*V[i_phylim, i_actlim])
t_stat   = diff_est / se_diff
@printf("phylim - actlim = %.6f  SE = %.6f  t = %.3f  p = %.4f\n",
        diff_est, se_diff, t_stat,
        2*(1 - cdf(Normal(), abs(t_stat))))
```

```{julia}
#=
*  Joint test of statistical significance of several variables
test phylim actlim totchr
=#

# test phylim actlim totchr
wald_test(reg1, ["phylim", "actlim", "totchr"]);
```

```{julia}
# Joint Wald test: phylim = actlim = totchr = 0
idx = [findfirst(==(n), cnames) for n in ["phylim","actlim","totchr"]]
βs  = β[idx]; Vs = V[idx, idx]
W = try
    βs' * LinearAlgebra.inv(Vs) * βs
catch
    NaN
end
@printf("Joint W = %.4f, df = %d, p = %.4f\n",
        W, length(idx), 1 - cdf(Chisq(length(idx)), W))
```

```{julia}
# Wald test of equality of coefficients: test phylim = actlim
# regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income, vce(robust)
m_wald = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3,
    @formula(ltotexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr + age + female + income),
    Vcov.robust())
β_w  = StatsBase.coef(m_wald)
V_w  = StatsBase.vcov(m_wald)
cn_w = StatsBase.coefnames(m_wald)
i_phy = findfirst(==("phylim"), cn_w)
i_act = findfirst(==("actlim"), cn_w)
# H0: phylim - actlim = 0  →  R = [0 ... 1 ... -1 ... 0], Rβ = β_phy - β_act
diff   = β_w[i_phy] - β_w[i_act]
var_diff = V_w[i_phy, i_phy] + V_w[i_act, i_act] - 2 * V_w[i_phy, i_act]
F_val  = diff^2 / var_diff
df_r   = m_wald.nobs - length(β_w)   # residual df
p_val  = 1 - cdf(FDist(1, df_r), F_val)
@printf(" ( 1)  phylim - actlim = 0\n\n")
@printf("       F(  1, %5d) = %7.2f\n", df_r, F_val)
@printf("            Prob > F = %8.4f\n", p_val)
```

```{julia}
wald_test(reg1, ["phylim", "actlim", "totchr"]);
```

```{julia}
#=
* Add a user-calculated statistic to the table
estimates drop REG1 REG2
quietly regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female ///
  income, vce(robust)
estadd scalar pvalue = Ftail(e(df_r),e(df_m),e(F))
estimates store REG1
quietly regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female ///
  educyr, vce(robust)
estadd scalar pvalue = Ftail(e(df_r),e(df_m),e(F))
estimates store REG2
esttab REG1 REG2, b(%10.4f) se scalars(F pvalue) mtitles keep(suppins) 
=#
# Add a user-calculated statistic (p-value of F-test) to the table
# estadd scalar pvalue = Ftail(e(df_r), e(df_m), e(F))
# Re-fit REG1 and REG2 with robust SEs and compute F p-values
REG1b = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3,
    @formula(ltotexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr + age + female + income),
    Vcov.robust())
REG2b = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3,
    @formula(ltotexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr + age + female + educyr),
    Vcov.robust())
for (label, m) in [("REG1", REG1b), ("REG2", REG2b)]
    fval = m.F
    df_m = length(coef(m)) - 1       # numerator df = number of regressors (excl. intercept)
    df_r = m.nobs - length(coef(m))   # denominator df
    pval = 1 - cdf(Distributions.FDist(df_m, df_r), fval)
    @printf("%s:  F = %.4f,  df_m = %d,  df_r = %d,  p-value = %.6f\n",
            label, fval, df_m, df_r, pval)
end
# Display comparison keeping only suppins, with F and p-value
RegressionTables.regtable(
    REG1b, REG2b;
    keep = ["suppins"],
    regression_statistics = [
        RegressionTables.FStat,
        RegressionTables.FStatPValue])
```

```{julia}
 i.famsze c.income#i.famsze, vce(robust) noheader allbaselevels
=#

reg_fact = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3,
```

```{julia}
#=
* Test joint significance of sets of indicator variables and interactions
testparm i.famsz c.income#i.famsze
=#
# Joint test of significance of famsze indicators + interactions
nm = StatsBase.coefnames(reg_fact)
idx_test = findall(n -> occursin("famsze_cat", n), nm)
βt = StatsBase.coef(reg_fact)[idx_test]
Vt = StatsBase.vcov(reg_fact)[idx_test, idx_test]
W = try
    βt' * LinearAlgebra.inv(Vt) * βt
catch

end
@printf("W = %.4f, df = %d, p = %.4f\n", W, length(idx_test),
        1 - cdf(Chisq(length(idx_test)), W))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Compute the average marginal effect in model with interactions
quietly regress totexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female c.income ///
 i.famsze c.income#i.famsze, vce(robust) noheader allbaselevels
margins, dydx(income)
=#
# testparm i.famsze c.income#i.famsze
# Joint robust Wald F-test. Build the design matrix manually to avoid
# collinearity issues from formula-based dummy expansion.
df3_tp = dropmissing(df3, [:ltotexp, :suppins, :phylim, :actlim, :totchr,
                            :age, :female, :income, :famsze_cat])

y_tp = Float64.(df3_tp.ltotexp)
# Base regressors (always included)
X_base = hcat(ones(nrow(df3_tp)),
              Float64.(df3_tp.suppins), Float64.(df3_tp.phylim),
              Float64.(df3_tp.actlim), Float64.(df3_tp.totchr),
              Float64.(df3_tp.age),    Float64.(df3_tp.female),
              Float64.(df3_tp.income))
cn_base = ["_cons","suppins","phylim","actlim","totchr","age","female","income"]

# Famsze dummies + income interactions (base level = 1, dropped)
fam_vals = [_rawval(v) for v in df3_tp.famsze_cat]
levs = sort(unique(fam_vals))
base_lev = levs[1]
test_levs = levs[levs .!= base_lev]

X_fam = zeros(nrow(df3_tp), 0)
cn_fam = String[]
# Dummies
for lv in test_levs
    X_fam = hcat(X_fam, Float64.(fam_vals .== lv))
    push!(cn_fam, "$(Int(lv)).famsze")
end
# Interactions income × famsze dummy
inc = Float64.(df3_tp.income)
for lv in test_levs
    col = Float64.(fam_vals .== lv) .* inc
    # Skip if the column is all zeros or has < 2 nonzero values (not estimable)
    if sum(col .!= 0) >= 2
        X_fam = hcat(X_fam, col)
        push!(cn_fam, "$(Int(lv)).famsze#c.income")
    end
end

X_full = hcat(X_base, X_fam)
cn_full = vcat(cn_base, cn_fam)
n_tp = size(X_full, 1); k_tp = size(X_full, 2)

# OLS
β_tp = X_full \ y_tp
u_tp = y_tp - X_full * β_tp

# HC1 robust sandwich
XtXinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(X_full' * X_full)
meat   = X_full' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(u_tp.^2) * X_full
V_hc1  = XtXinv * meat * XtXinv * (n_tp / (n_tp - k_tp))

# Test indices: all famsze-related columns
idx_fam_test = (length(cn_base)+1):k_tp
q    = length(idx_fam_test)
βtp  = β_tp[idx_fam_test]
Vtp  = V_hc1[idx_fam_test, idx_fam_test]
df_r = n_tp - k_tp

F_tp = (βtp' * LinearAlgebra.inv(Vtp) * βtp) / q
p_tp = 1 - cdf(FDist(q, df_r), F_tp)
@printf("testparm i.famsze c.income#i.famsze\n")
for (j, i) in enumerate(idx_fam_test)
    @printf(" (%2d)  %-35s = 0\n", j, cn_full[i])
end
@printf("\n       F(%d, %d) = %7.2f\n", q, df_r, F_tp)
@printf("            Prob > F = %8.4f\n", p_tp)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Compute elasticity for a specified regressor
quietly regress totexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income, vce(robust)
margins, eyex(totchr) atmean
=#
# Average marginal effect of income (numerical derivative)
function ame_income(model, df, varname; h = 0.01)
    df_p = copy(df); df_p[!, varname] .= df_p[!, varname] .+ h
    df_m = copy(df); df_m[!, varname] .= df_m[!, varname] .- h
    mean(FixedEffectModels.predict(model, df_p) .- FixedEffectModels.predict(model, df_m)) / (2h)
end
m_lin = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3, @formula(totexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr +
                                   age + female + income), Vcov.robust(); save = :all)
@printf("AME of income = %.4f\n", ame_income(m_lin, df3, :income))
```

### 3.5.3 Influential observations

```{julia}
#=
* Compute dfits that combines outliers and leverage
quietly regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income
predict dfits, dfits
scalar threshold = 2*sqrt((e(df_m)+1)/e(N))
display "dfits threshold = "  %6.3f threshold
tabstat dfits, stat (min p1 p5 p95 p99 max) format(%9.3f) col(stat)
=#
# DFITS-like influence measure (manual via leverage and residuals)
# DFITS_i = t_i * sqrt(h_i / (1 - h_i))
y = df3_diag.ltotexp
X = hcat(ones(nrow(df3_diag)),
         df3_diag.suppins, df3_diag.phylim, df3_diag.actlim,
         df3_diag.totchr, df3_diag.age, df3_diag.female, df3_diag.income)
H = try
    X * LinearAlgebra.inv(X'X) * X'
catch
    # Use pseudoinverse fallback when X'X is singular.
    X * LinearAlgebra.pinv(X'X) * X'
end
h = diag(H)
σ² = sum(uhat.^2) / (length(y) - size(X, 2))
t_resid = uhat ./ sqrt.(σ² .* (1 .- h))
dfits = t_resid .* sqrt.(h ./ (1 .- h))

threshold = 2 * sqrt((size(X, 2)) / nrow(df3_diag))
@printf("DFITS threshold = %.3f\n", threshold)
@printf("min=%.3f  p1=%.3f  p99=%.3f  max=%.3f\n",
        minimum(dfits), quantile(dfits, 0.01),
        quantile(dfits, 0.99), maximum(dfits))
```

```{julia}
#=
list dfits totexp ltotexp yhat uhat if abs(dfits) > 2*threshold & e(sample), clean
=#
# list dfits totexp ltotexp yhat uhat if abs(dfits) > 2*threshold & e(sample)
influential = findall(abs.(dfits) .> 2 * threshold)
if isempty(influential)
    println("No observations exceed 2×threshold = $(round(2*threshold, digits=3))")
else
    listing = DataFrame(
        obs     = influential,
        dfits   = dfits[influential],
        totexp  = df3_diag.totexp[influential],
        ltotexp = df3_diag.ltotexp[influential],
        yhat    = yhat[influential],
        uhat    = uhat[influential])
    sort!(listing, :dfits, by=abs, rev=true)
    _pt_compat(listing; formatters=PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.3f", 2:6))
end
```

#### Test of the functional form of the conditional mean

```{julia}
#=
* Variable augmentation test of conditional mean using estat ovtest
quietly regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female ///
  income, vce(robust)
estat ovtest
=#
# Ramsey RESET test: regress y on X plus powers of fitted values
yhat_diag = FixedEffectModels.predict(m_diag, df3_diag)
df3_diag.yhat2 = yhat_diag.^2
df3_diag.yhat3 = yhat_diag.^3
df3_diag.yhat4 = yhat_diag.^4
m_reset = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3_diag,
    @formula(ltotexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr + age + female +
                       income + yhat2 + yhat3 + yhat4))
nm = StatsBase.coefnames(m_reset)
idx_p = findall(n -> n in ("yhat2","yhat3","yhat4"), nm)
βp = StatsBase.coef(m_reset)[idx_p]; Vp = StatsBase.vcov(m_reset)[idx_p, idx_p]
F = try
    (βp' * LinearAlgebra.inv(Vp) * βp) / 3
catch
    NaN
end
@printf("RESET F(3, %d) = %.3f, p = %.4f\n",
        dof_residual(m_reset), F, 1 - cdf(FDist(3, dof_residual(m_reset)), F))
```

```{julia}

* Link test of functional form of conditional mean

linktest

println(m_link)
```

### 3.5.5 Tests have power in more than one direction

```{julia}
# Simulation: y = exp(1 + 0.25x + 4x²) + u, fit y on x + x²
Random.seed!(10101)
N = 50
x = rand(N)
u = randn(N)
y = exp.(1 .+ 0.25 .* x .+ 4 .* x.^2) .+ u
xsq = x.^2
df_sim = DataFrame(y = y, x = x, xsq = xsq)
m_sim = FixedEffectModels.reg(df_sim, @formula(y ~ x + xsq))
println(m_sim)
```

```{julia}
# Heteroskedasticity test on the simulated model
yhat_sim = FixedEffectModels.predict(m_sim, df_sim)
uh_sim   = df_sim.y .- yhat_sim
df_sim.uh2 = uh_sim.^2
m_bp_sim = FixedEffectModels.reg(df_sim, @formula(uh2 ~ x + xsq))
LMs = nrow(df_sim) * StatsBase.r2(m_bp_sim)
@printf("BP LM = %.3f, p = %.4f\n", LMs, 1 - cdf(Chisq(2), LMs))
```

```{julia}
# RESET on simulated model
df_sim.yh2 = yhat_sim.^2
df_sim.yh3 = yhat_sim.^3
m_reset_sim = FixedEffectModels.reg(df_sim, @formula(y ~ x + xsq + yh2 + yh3))
nm = StatsBase.coefnames(m_reset_sim)
idx_p = findall(n -> n in ("yh2","yh3"), nm)
βp = StatsBase.coef(m_reset_sim)[idx_p]; Vp = StatsBase.vcov(m_reset_sim)[idx_p, idx_p]
F = try
    (βp' * LinearAlgebra.inv(Vp) * βp) / 2
catch
    NaN
end
@printf("RESET F(2, %d) = %.3f, p = %.4f\n",
        dof_residual(m_reset_sim), F,
        1 - cdf(FDist(2, dof_residual(m_reset_sim)), F))
```

### 3.6.1 In-sample prediction

```{julia}

regress totexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income, vce(robust)

df3pos = filter(r -> r.totexp > 0, df3)
m_levels = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3pos,
    @formula(totexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr + age + female + income),
    Vcov.robust(); save = :all)
println(m_levels)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Prediction in model linear in levels
predict yhatlevels
summarize totexp yhatlevels
=#
# Predicted values vs observed
df3pos_clean = dropmissing(df3pos[:, [:totexp, :suppins, :phylim, :actlim,
                                       :totchr, :age, :female, :income]])
yhat_lev = FixedEffectModels.predict(m_levels, df3pos_clean)
@printf("totexp:     mean = %.2f\n", mean(df3pos_clean.totexp))
@printf("yhatlevels: mean = %.2f\n", mean(yhat_lev))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Compare median prediction and median actual value
tabstat totexp yhatlevels, stat (count p50) col(stat)
=#
# Compare medians
@printf("totexp     median = %.2f  (N=%d)\n",
        median(df3pos_clean.totexp), nrow(df3pos_clean))
@printf("yhatlevels median = %.2f\n", median(yhat_lev))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Compute standard errors of prediction and forecast with default VCE
quietly regress totexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income
predict yhatstdp, stdp
predict yhatstdf, stdf
summarize yhatstdp yhatstdf
=#
# Standard errors of prediction (stdp) and forecast (stdf)
X = Matrix(hcat(ones(nrow(df3pos_clean)),
                df3pos_clean.suppins, df3pos_clean.phylim,
                df3pos_clean.actlim,  df3pos_clean.totchr,
                df3pos_clean.age,     df3pos_clean.female,
                df3pos_clean.income))
V_β = StatsBase.vcov(m_levels)
σ²  = sum((df3pos_clean.totexp .- yhat_lev).^2) / dof_residual(m_levels)
stdp = [sqrt(x'V_β*x) for x in eachrow(X)]
stdf = sqrt.(stdp.^2 .+ σ²)
@printf("stdp: mean = %.4f\n", mean(stdp))
@printf("stdf: mean = %.4f\n", mean(stdf))
```


```{julia}
# Compute standard errors of prediction and forecast with default VCE
# regress totexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income
# predict yhatstdp, stdp
# predict yhatstdf, stdf
# summarize yhatstdp yhatstdf
xvars_pred = [:suppins, :phylim, :actlim, :totchr, :age, :female, :income]
df3_pred = dropmissing(df3[:, vcat([:totexp], xvars_pred)])
# Unwrap any LabeledValue types and convert to Float64
for c in vcat([:totexp], xvars_pred)
    df3_pred[!, c] = Float64.([_rawval(v) for v in df3_pred[!, c]])
end
@printf("N = %d\n", nrow(df3_pred))

m_pred = GLM.lm(@formula(totexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr + age + female + income),
                df3_pred)
Xm_pred = GLM.modelmatrix(m_pred)
n_pred  = nrow(df3_pred)
k_pred  = size(Xm_pred, 2)
yhat_p  = GLM.predict(m_pred)
e_pred  = Float64.(df3_pred.totexp) .- yhat_p
sig2_ols = sum(e_pred.^2) / (n_pred - k_pred)         # σ̂² = RSS/(n-k)
XtXinv  = LinearAlgebra.inv(Xm_pred' * Xm_pred)       # (X'X)⁻¹

# stdp = SE of fitted value = σ̂ · sqrt(xᵢ'(X'X)⁻¹xᵢ)
# stdf = SE of forecast     = sqrt(σ̂² + σ̂² · xᵢ'(X'X)⁻¹xᵢ) = σ̂ · sqrt(1 + xᵢ'(X'X)⁻¹xᵢ)
yhatstdp = [sqrt(sig2_ols * dot(x, XtXinv * x)) for x in eachrow(Xm_pred)]
yhatstdf = [sqrt(sig2_ols * (1.0 + dot(x, XtXinv * x))) for x in eachrow(Xm_pred)]

@printf("Root MSE = %.4f\n", sqrt(sig2_ols))
println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
println("-------------+---------------------------------------------------------")
@printf("    yhatstdp | %10d  %10.1f  %10.4f  %10.4f  %10.3f\n",
        n_pred, mean(yhatstdp), std(yhatstdp), minimum(yhatstdp), maximum(yhatstdp))
@printf("    yhatstdf | %10d  %10.2f  %10.5f  %10.2f  %10.1f\n",
        n_pred, mean(yhatstdf), std(yhatstdf), minimum(yhatstdf), maximum(yhatstdf))
```

### 3.6.3 Prediction in logs: The retransformation problem

```{julia}
#=
* Prediction in levels from a logarithmic model
quietly regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income
quietly predict lyhat
generate yhatwrong = exp(lyhat)
generate yhatnormal = exp(lyhat)*exp(0.5*e(rmse)^2)
quietly predict uhat, residual
generate expuhat = exp(uhat)
quietly summarize expuhat
generate yhatduan = r(mean)*exp(lyhat) 
summarize totexp yhatwrong yhatnormal yhatduan yhatlevels
=#
# Log model: prediction in levels using normal vs Duan smearing
m_log = FixedEffectModels.reg(df3pos, @formula(ltotexp ~ suppins + phylim + actlim + totchr +
                                       age + female + income); save = :all)
df3pos_log = dropmissing(df3pos[:, [:totexp, :ltotexp, :suppins, :phylim,
                                     :actlim, :totchr, :age, :female, :income]])
lyhat = FixedEffectModels.predict(m_log, df3pos_log)
uhat  = df3pos_log.ltotexp .- lyhat
σ²    = sum(uhat.^2) / dof_residual(m_log)

yhatwrong  = exp.(lyhat)
yhatnormal = exp.(lyhat) .* exp(0.5 * σ²)        # log-normal correction
yhatduan   = mean(exp.(uhat)) .* exp.(lyhat)     # Duan smearing
@printf("totexp     mean = %.2f\n", mean(df3pos_log.totexp))
@printf("yhatwrong  mean = %.2f\n", mean(yhatwrong))
@printf("yhatnormal mean = %.2f\n", mean(yhatnormal))
@printf("yhatduan   mean = %.2f\n", mean(yhatduan))
```

```{julia}
summarize_stata(df3pos_log, [:totexp])
```

### 3.6.4 Prediction exercise

```{julia}
#=
* Predicted effect of supplementary insurance: methods 1 and 2
bysort suppins: summarize totexp yhatlevels yhatduan
=#
# Predicted effect of supplementary insurance: by-group means
df3pos_log.yhatnormal = yhatnormal
df3pos_log.yhatduan   = yhatduan
combine(groupby(df3pos_log, :suppins),
    :totexp     => mean,
    :yhatnormal => mean,
    :yhatduan   => mean)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Predicted effect of supplementary insurance: method 3 for log-linear model
quietly regress ltotexp suppins phylim actlim totchr age female income
preserve
quietly replace suppins = 1
quietly predict lyhat1
generate yhatnormal1 = exp(lyhat1)*exp(0.5*e(rmse)^2) 
quietly replace suppins = 0
quietly predict lyhat0 
generate yhatnormal0 = exp(lyhat0)*exp(0.5*e(rmse)^2) 
generate treateffect = yhatnormal1 - yhatnormal0
summarize yhatnormal1 yhatnormal0 treateffect 
restore
=#
# Treatment effect via counterfactual prediction (suppins=1 vs 0)
df1 = copy(df3pos_log); df1.suppins .= 1
df0 = copy(df3pos_log); df0.suppins .= 0
ly1 = FixedEffectModels.predict(m_log, df1)
ly0 = FixedEffectModels.predict(m_log, df0)
yh1 = exp.(ly1) .* exp(0.5 * σ²)
yh0 = exp.(ly0) .* exp(0.5 * σ²)
@printf("E[y|x,suppins=1] = %.2f\n", mean(yh1))
@printf("E[y|x,suppins=0] = %.2f\n", mean(yh0))
@printf("Treatment effect = %.2f\n", mean(yh1 .- yh0))
```

## 3.8 OLS using native Julia (matrix algebra)

```{julia}
# OLS with White robust SE — native Julia, equivalent to the Mata example
df3pos = filter(r -> r.totexp > 0, df3)
df3p   = dropmissing(df3pos[:, [:ltotexp, :suppins, :phylim, :actlim,
                                 :totchr, :age, :female, :income]])
y = df3p.ltotexp
X = Matrix(hcat(df3p.suppins, df3p.phylim, df3p.actlim, df3p.totchr,
                df3p.age, df3p.female, df3p.income, ones(nrow(df3p))))
xnames = ["suppins","phylim","actlim","totchr","age","female","income","_cons"]

n, k    = size(X)
XtX_inv = try
    LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(X'X)))
catch
    LinearAlgebra.pinv(X'X)  # Use pseudoinverse for singular matrices
end
b       = XtX_inv * X' * y
e       = y .- X*b
s2      = (e'e) / (n - k)
V_def   = s2 .* XtX_inv                                     # default VCE (unused)
V_white = XtX_inv * (X' * Diagonal(e.^2) * X) * XtX_inv * (n / (n - k))   # robust

se = sqrt.(diag(V_white))
println("─" ^ 70)
@printf("%-10s %12s %12s %8s %8s\n", "", "Coef.", "Rob.SE", "t", "P>|t|")
println("─" ^ 70)
for i in 1:k
    t = b[i] / se[i]
    p = 2 * (1 - cdf(Normal(), abs(t)))
    @printf("%-10s %12.6f %12.6f %8.2f %8.4f\n", xnames[i], b[i], se[i], t, p)
end
println("─" ^ 70)
@printf("N = %d, k = %d, R² = %.4f\n",
        n, k, 1 - sum(e.^2)/sum((y .- mean(y)).^2))
```

```{julia}
                                female + income), Vcov.robust())
```
